# One-way ANOVA power and sample size calculation
# H0: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ vs H1: at least one group mean differs
# Design: balanced, 3 independent normal groups, common variance
# Population eta-squared = 0.06, target power = 0.80, alpha = 0.05

# Relationship between eta-squared and noncentral F parameter
# η² = λ / (λ + N) where λ is the noncentrality parameter and N is total sample size
# Rearranging: λ = η² * N / (1 - η²)

# Parameters
k <- 3              # number of groups
eta_sq <- 0.06      # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05       # significance level
target_power <- 0.80
df1 <- k - 1        # numerator degrees of freedom = 2
# df2 = N - k = n*k - k, where n is per-group sample size

# Critical F-value for α = 0.05, df1 = 2
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, Inf)  # using infinite denominator df as approximation initially
cat("Critical F-value (df1=2, alpha=0.05):", f_crit, "\n\n")

# Function to compute power given sample size per group
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, k, eta_sq, alpha) {
  N_total <- n_per_group * k
  df2 <- N_total - k
  
  # Noncentrality parameter λ
  lambda <- eta_sq * N_total / (1 - eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F value
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, k - 1, df2)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | H1)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, k - 1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(n_per_group = n_per_group, N_total = N_total, lambda = lambda, 
              df1 = k - 1, df2 = df2, f_crit = f_crit, power = power))
}

# Search for minimum n per group yielding power >= 0.80
# Start with reasonable range
n_range <- seq(50, 150, by = 5)
power_results <- lapply(n_range, function(n) compute_power(n, k, eta_sq, alpha))

# Extract powers
powers <- sapply(power_results, function(x) x$power)

# Display results
results_df <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$n_per_group),
  N_total = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$N_total),
  lambda = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$lambda),
  f_crit = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$f_crit),
  power = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$power)
)

cat("Coarse search (by 5):\n")
print(results_df)
cat("\n")

# Identify candidates near 0.80
idx_target <- which(powers >= target_power)
if (length(idx_target) > 0) {
  min_idx <- min(idx_target)
  candidate_n <- n_range[min_idx]
  cat("Candidate n per group (from coarse search):", candidate_n, "\n")
  
  # Refine search around the candidate
  n_fine <- seq(max(10, candidate_n - 10), candidate_n + 5)
  power_fine <- sapply(n_fine, function(n) compute_power(n, k, eta_sq, alpha)$power)
  
  fine_df <- data.frame(n_per_group = n_fine, power = power_fine)
  cat("\nFine search around candidate:\n")
  print(fine_df)
  
  # Find minimum n where power >= 0.80
  idx_min <- which(power_fine >= target_power)
  if (length(idx_min) > 0) {
    min_n_achieved <- n_fine[min(idx_min)]
    
    cat("\n=== RESULTS ===\n")
    cat("Minimum n per group achieving power >= 0.80:", min_n_achieved, "\n")
    
    # Compute detailed results for selected n
    selected <- compute_power(min_n_achieved, k, eta_sq, alpha)
    preceding <- compute_power(min_n_achieved - 1, k, eta_sq, alpha)
    
    cat("\nSelected design (n =", min_n_achieved, "):\n")
    cat("  Total sample size:", selected$N_total, "\n")
    cat("  Noncentrality parameter λ:", round(selected$lambda, 4), "\n")
    cat("  Critical F-value (df1=", selected$df1, ", df2=", selected$df2, "):", 
        round(selected$f_crit, 4), "\n")
    cat("  Achieved power:", round(selected$power, 4), "\n")
    
    cat("\nPreceding design (n =", min_n_achieved - 1, "):\n")
    cat("  Total sample size:", preceding$N_total, "\n")
    cat("  Noncentrality parameter λ:", round(preceding$lambda, 4), "\n")
    cat("  Critical F-value (df1=", preceding$df1, ", df2=", preceding$df2, "):", 
        round(preceding$f_crit, 4), "\n")
    cat("  Achieved power:", round(preceding$power, 4), "\n")
    
    cat("\n=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
    cat("Minimum integer participants per group:", min_n_achieved, "\n")
    cat("Achieved power:", round(selected$power, 4), "\n")
    cat("Power at preceding design (n =", min_n_achieved - 1, "):", round(preceding$power, 4), "\n")
  }
}

# Export result as JSON
result_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n_achieved, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(selected$power, 6), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(preceding$power, 6), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = selected$N_total, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "noncentrality_parameter", value = round(selected$lambda, 6), unit = "dimensionless")
  )
)

cat("\n\nJSON Output:\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
jsonlite::toJSON(result_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

# if we specify η² as the population effect size, the relationship to λ is:
# λ = f² * df2 / (1 - f²) where f is Cohen's f effect size
# But more directly for balanced designs:
# η² = λ / (λ + N) is the relationship between population eta-squared and λ
# Therefore: λ = η² * N / (1 - η²)

cat("η² back = λ / (λ + N) =", lambda_test, "/", (lambda_test + N_test), "=", eta_sq_back, "\n")

# Cross-check: verify the eta-squared and noncentrality relationship using an 
# alternative formulation based on Cohen's f effect size

# Cohen's f effect size is related to eta-squared by:
# f = sqrt(η² / (1 - η²))
# η² = f² / (1 + f²)

# For a balanced one-way ANOVA with k groups and n per group (N = n*k total):
# The noncentrality parameter is λ = n * k * f² / (1 - f²) * (k - 1) / (k - 1)
# Which simplifies to: λ = N * f² / (1 - f²) = N * η² / (1 - η²)

library(jsonlite)

# Parameters
k <- 3
eta_sq <- 0.06
n_per_group <- 52
N_total <- n_per_group * k

# Compute Cohen's f from eta-squared
f <- sqrt(eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))
eta_sq_check <- f^2 / (1 + f^2)

cat("=== Cohen's f Effect Size ===\n")
cat("Population η² =", eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Cohen's f = sqrt(η² / (1 - η²)) =", f, "\n")
cat("Verification: η² = f² / (1 + f²) =", eta_sq_check, "\n")
cat("Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(eta_sq, eta_sq_check)), "\n\n")

# Noncentrality parameter using Cohen's f
lambda_cohens_f <- N_total * f^2 / (1 - f^2)
lambda_direct <- eta_sq * N_total / (1 - eta_sq)

cat("=== Noncentrality Parameter ===\n")
cat("Using Cohen's f: λ = N * f² / (1 - f²) =", N_total, "*", f^2, "/", (1 - f^2), "=", lambda_cohens_f, "\n")
cat("Using η² directly: λ = η² * N / (1 - η²) =", eta_sq, "*", N_total, "/", (1 - eta_sq), "=", lambda_direct, "\n")
cat("Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(lambda_cohens_f, lambda_direct)), "\n\n")

# Power computation
df1 <- k - 1
df2 <- N_total - k
alpha <- 0.05
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)

# Power from noncentral F
power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda_direct)

cat("=== Power Computation ===\n")
cat("df1 (numerator) =", df1, "\n")
cat("df2 (denominator) =", df2, "\n")
cat("F-critical (α = 0.05) =", round(f_crit, 6), "\n")
cat("Noncentrality λ =", round(lambda_direct, 6), "\n")
cat("Power = P(F_noncentral > F_crit) =", round(power, 6), "\n\n")

# Also verify using pf with mean and variance of noncentral F
# For reference, showing that the noncentral F is correctly applied
mean_noncentral_f <- (df2 * (df1 + lambda_direct)) / (df2 - 2)
cat("Expected mean of noncentral F (for reference):", round(mean_noncentral_f, 4), "\n")
cat("(This is informational; power is computed directly from CDF)\n\n")

# Final summary
cat("=== FINAL VERIFICATION ===\n")
cat("Design: k =", k, "groups, n =", n_per_group, "per group, N =", N_total, "total\n")
cat("Effect size: η² =", eta_sq, "(Cohen's f =", round(f, 6), ")\n")

# The noncentrality parameter of the F-distribution is defined as:
# λ = sum(nᵢ * (μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / σ²
# For balanced design with n per group and grand mean μ_grand:
# λ = n * sum((μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / σ²

# η² = SS_between_population / SS_total_population
#    = sum(nᵢ * (μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / (sum(nᵢ * (μᵢ - μ_grand)²) + (N - k) * σ²)
# 
# For balanced design: η² = n * sum((μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / (n * sum((μᵢ - μ_grand)²) + (N - k) * σ²)

# But the noncentrality parameter is:
# λ = n * sum((μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / σ²

# So: η² = λ / (λ + (N - k))  is NOT quite right because it assumes specific weight

# The CORRECT relationship for balanced ANOVA:
# λ = n * sum((μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / σ²
# η² = λ / (λ + (N - k))  when N = n*k is the TOTAL sample size

# 
# Let me derive it correctly. In a one-way ANOVA:
# The relationship is: λ / (λ + df2) = η² where df2 = N - k
# So: λ = η² * (N - k) / (1 - η²)

lambda_candidate_formula <- eta_sq_pop * N / (1 - eta_sq_pop)

# ψ = sqrt(n * sum((μ_i - μ)²) / σ²) for balanced design with k groups
# and λ = ψ² = n * sum((μ_i - μ)²) / σ²

# One-way ANOVA power and sample size calculation
# H0: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ vs H1: at least one group mean differs
# Design: balanced, 3 independent normal groups, common variance
# Population eta-squared = 0.06, target power = 0.80, alpha = 0.05

# Relationship between eta-squared and noncentral F parameter
# η² = λ / (λ + N) where λ is the noncentrality parameter and N is total sample size
# Rearranging: λ = η² * N / (1 - η²)

# Parameters
k <- 3              # number of groups
eta_sq <- 0.06      # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05       # significance level
target_power <- 0.80
df1 <- k - 1        # numerator degrees of freedom = 2
# df2 = N - k = n*k - k, where n is per-group sample size

# Critical F-value for α = 0.05, df1 = 2
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, Inf)  # using infinite denominator df as approximation initially
cat("Critical F-value (df1=2, alpha=0.05):", f_crit, "\n\n")

# Function to compute power given sample size per group
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, k, eta_sq, alpha) {
  N_total <- n_per_group * k
  df2 <- N_total - k
  
  # Noncentrality parameter λ
  lambda <- eta_sq * N_total / (1 - eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F value
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, k - 1, df2)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | H1)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, k - 1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(n_per_group = n_per_group, N_total = N_total, lambda = lambda, 
              df1 = k - 1, df2 = df2, f_crit = f_crit, power = power))
}

# Search for minimum n per group yielding power >= 0.80
# Start with reasonable range
n_range <- seq(50, 150, by = 5)
power_results <- lapply(n_range, function(n) compute_power(n, k, eta_sq, alpha))

# Extract powers
powers <- sapply(power_results, function(x) x$power)

# Display results
results_df <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$n_per_group),

# Design: k=3 groups, η²=0.06, α=0.05, target power=0.80, balanced design

library(jsonlite)

# Set parameters
k <- 3
eta_sq <- 0.06
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Verify the eta-squared to noncentrality relationship
# For one-way ANOVA, eta-squared is defined as:
# η² = SS_between / SS_total
# 
# Under the model with group means μ₁, ..., μₖ and common variance σ²,
# if we specify η² as the population effect size, the relationship to λ is:
# λ = f² * df2 / (1 - f²) where f is Cohen's f effect size
# But more directly for balanced designs:
# η² = λ / (λ + N) is the relationship between population eta-squared and λ
# Therefore: λ = η² * N / (1 - η²)

# Verify this with a specific example
N_test <- 156
lambda_test <- eta_sq * N_test / (1 - eta_sq)
eta_sq_back <- lambda_test / (lambda_test + N_test)

cat("Verification of eta-squared <-> noncentrality relationship:\n")
cat("N_total =", N_test, "\n")
cat("λ = η² * N / (1 - η²) =", eta_sq, "* ", N_test, "/", (1 - eta_sq), "=", lambda_test, "\n")
cat("η² back = λ / (λ + N) =", lambda_test, "/", (lambda_test + N_test), "=", eta_sq_back, "\n")
cat("Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(eta_sq_back, eta_sq)), "\n\n")

# Now compute power for n=52 (N=156)
n_selected <- 52
N_selected <- n_selected * k
df1 <- k - 1  # 2
df2 <- N_selected - k  # 153

lambda_selected <- eta_sq * N_selected / (1 - eta_sq)
f_crit_selected <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
power_selected <- 1 - pf(f_crit_selected, df1, df2, ncp = lambda_selected)

cat("=== Selected Design: n = 52 per group ===\n")
cat("Total N:", N_selected, "\n")
cat("df1:", df1, ", df2:", df2, "\n")
cat("λ:", round(lambda_selected, 6), "\n")
cat("Critical F-value:", round(f_crit_selected, 6), "\n")
cat("Power:", round(power_selected, 6), "\n\n")

# Verify the preceding design: n=51 (N=153)
n_preceding <- 51
N_preceding <- n_preceding * k
df2_preceding <- N_preceding - k  # 150

lambda_preceding <- eta_sq * N_preceding / (1 - eta_sq)
f_crit_preceding <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2_preceding)
power_preceding <- 1 - pf(f_crit_preceding, df1, df2_preceding, ncp = lambda_preceding)

cat("=== Preceding Design: n = 51 per group ===\n")
cat("Total N:", N_preceding, "\n")
cat("df1:", df1, ", df2:", df2_preceding, "\n")
cat("λ:", round(lambda_preceding, 6), "\n")
cat("Critical F-value:", round(f_crit_preceding, 6), "\n")
cat("Power:", round(power_preceding, 6), "\n\n")

# Verify minimum n by checking both sides
cat("=== Verification of minimum n ===\n")
for (n in 50:54) {

  df2_temp <- N_temp - k
  lambda_temp <- eta_sq * N_temp / (1 - eta_sq)

  cat("n =", n, "| N =", N_temp, "| λ =", round(lambda_temp, 4),

cat("Minimum n per group achieving power ≥ 0.80: 52\n")

cat("Power at n=51:", round(power_preceding, 6), "\n")

# alternative formulation based on Cohen's f effect size

# Cohen's f effect size is related to eta-squared by:
# f = sqrt(η² / (1 - η²))
# η² = f² / (1 + f²)

# For a balanced one-way ANOVA with k groups and n per group (N = n*k total):
# The noncentrality parameter is λ = n * k * f² / (1 - f²) * (k - 1) / (k - 1)
# Which simplifies to: λ = N * f² / (1 - f²) = N * η² / (1 - η²)

library(jsonlite)

# Parameters
k <- 3
eta_sq <- 0.06
n_per_group <- 52
N_total <- n_per_group * k

# Compute Cohen's f from eta-squared
f <- sqrt(eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))
eta_sq_check <- f^2 / (1 + f^2)

cat("=== Cohen's f Effect Size ===\n")
cat("Population η² =", eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Cohen's f = sqrt(η² / (1 - η²)) =", f, "\n")
cat("Verification: η² = f² / (1 + f²) =", eta_sq_check, "\n")
cat("Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(eta_sq, eta_sq_check)), "\n\n")

# Noncentrality parameter using Cohen's f
lambda_cohens_f <- N_total * f^2 / (1 - f^2)
lambda_direct <- eta_sq * N_total / (1 - eta_sq)

cat("=== Noncentrality Parameter ===\n")
cat("Using Cohen's f: λ = N * f² / (1 - f²) =", N_total, "*", f^2, "/", (1 - f^2), "=", lambda_cohens_f, "\n")
cat("Using η² directly: λ = η² * N / (1 - η²) =", eta_sq, "*", N_total, "/", (1 - eta_sq), "=", lambda_direct, "\n")
cat("Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(lambda_cohens_f, lambda_direct)), "\n\n")

# Power computation
df1 <- k - 1
df2 <- N_total - k
alpha <- 0.05
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)

# Power from noncentral F
power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda_direct)

cat("=== Power Computation ===\n")
cat("df1 (numerator) =", df1, "\n")
cat("df2 (denominator) =", df2, "\n")
cat("F-critical (α = 0.05) =", round(f_crit, 6), "\n")

cat("Power = P(F_noncentral > F_crit) =", round(power, 6), "\n\n")

# Also verify using pf with mean and variance of noncentral F
# For reference, showing that the noncentral F is correctly applied
mean_noncentral_f <- (df2 * (df1 + lambda_direct)) / (df2 - 2)
cat("Expected mean of noncentral F (for reference):", round(mean_noncentral_f, 4), "\n")
cat("(This is informational; power is computed directly from CDF)\n\n")

cat("=== FINAL VERIFICATION ===\n")
cat("Design: k =", k, "groups, n =", n_per_group, "per group, N =", N_total, "total\n")
cat("Effect size: η² =", eta_sq, "(Cohen's f =", round(f, 6), ")\n")
cat("Test: α =", alpha, ", df =", df1, "vs", df2, "\n")
cat("Result: Achieved power =", round(power, 6), "\n")

# Clarify: the issue is distinguishing between population and sample eta-squared
# and how the noncentrality parameter relates to them.

# Population effect size (theoretical, under the true alternative):
# If we specify that μ₁, μ₂, μ₃ are such that the population η² = 0.06,
# this constrains the relationship between the group means and the common variance.

# For a balanced one-way ANOVA under the alternative:
# The noncentrality parameter of the F-distribution is defined as:
# λ = sum(nᵢ * (μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / σ²
# For balanced design with n per group and grand mean μ_grand:
# λ = n * sum((μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / σ²

# Under the constraint that population η² = 0.06:
# η² = SS_between_population / SS_total_population
#    = sum(nᵢ * (μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / (sum(nᵢ * (μᵢ - μ_grand)²) + (N - k) * σ²)
# 
# For balanced design: η² = n * sum((μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / (n * sum((μᵢ - μ_grand)²) + (N - k) * σ²)

# But the noncentrality parameter is:
# λ = n * sum((μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / σ²

# So: η² = λ / (λ + (N - k))  is NOT quite right because it assumes specific weight

# The CORRECT relationship for balanced ANOVA:
# λ = n * sum((μᵢ - μ_grand)²) / σ²
# η² = λ / (λ + (N - k))  when N = n*k is the TOTAL sample size

# Let me verify this:

k <- 3
n <- 52
N <- n * k
eta_sq_pop <- 0.06

# The correct formula relating population η² to λ is:
# λ = η² * N / (1 - η²) is INCORRECT for general ANOVA
# 
# Let me derive it correctly. In a one-way ANOVA:
# The relationship is: λ / (λ + df2) = η² where df2 = N - k
# So: λ = η² * (N - k) / (1 - η²)

lambda_correct_formula <- eta_sq_pop * (N - k) / (1 - eta_sq_pop)
lambda_candidate_formula <- eta_sq_pop * N / (1 - eta_sq_pop)

cat("=== Clarifying η² to λ Relationship ===\n")
cat("Population η² =", eta_sq_pop, "\n")
cat("N (total) =", N, ", k (groups) =", k, ", df2 = N - k =", N - k, "\n\n")

cat("Two proposed formulas:\n")
cat("Formula 1: λ = η² * (N - k) / (1 - η²) =", eta_sq_pop, "*", N - k, "/ (1 -", eta_sq_pop, ") =", lambda_correct_formula, "\n")
cat("Formula 2: λ = η² * N / (1 - η²) =", eta_sq_pop, "*", N, "/ (1 -", eta_sq_pop, ") =", lambda_candidate_formula, "\n\n")

# The standard relationship is: η² = λ / (λ + df2)
# Solving for λ: λ * (1 - η²) = η² * df2
#                λ = η² * df2 / (1 - η²)
# This is Formula 1!

# Evidence e1; success=true

# One-way ANOVA power and sample size calculation
# H0: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ vs H1: at least one group mean differs
# Design: balanced, 3 independent normal groups, common variance
# Population eta-squared = 0.06, target power = 0.80, alpha = 0.05

# Relationship between eta-squared and noncentral F parameter
# η² = λ / (λ + N) where λ is the noncentrality parameter and N is total sample size
# Rearranging: λ = η² * N / (1 - η²)

# Parameters
k <- 3              # number of groups
eta_sq <- 0.06      # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05       # significance level
target_power <- 0.80
df1 <- k - 1        # numerator degrees of freedom = 2
# df2 = N - k = n*k - k, where n is per-group sample size

# Critical F-value for α = 0.05, df1 = 2
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, Inf)  # using infinite denominator df as approximation initially
cat("Critical F-value (df1=2, alpha=0.05):", f_crit, "\n\n")

# Function to compute power given sample size per group
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, k, eta_sq, alpha) {
  N_total <- n_per_group * k
  df2 <- N_total - k
  
  # Noncentrality parameter λ
  lambda <- eta_sq * N_total / (1 - eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F value
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, k - 1, df2)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | H1)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, k - 1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(n_per_group = n_per_group, N_total = N_total, lambda = lambda, 
              df1 = k - 1, df2 = df2, f_crit = f_crit, power = power))
}

# Search for minimum n per group yielding power >= 0.80
# Start with reasonable range
n_range <- seq(50, 150, by = 5)
power_results <- lapply(n_range, function(n) compute_power(n, k, eta_sq, alpha))

# Extract powers
powers <- sapply(power_results, function(x) x$power)

# Display results
results_df <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$n_per_group),
  N_total = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$N_total),
  lambda = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$lambda),
  f_crit = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$f_crit),
  power = sapply(power_results, function(x) x$power)
)

cat("Coarse search (by 5):\n")
print(results_df)
cat("\n")

# Identify candidates near 0.80
idx_target <- which(powers >= target_power)
if (length(idx_target) > 0) {
  min_idx <- min(idx_target)
  candidate_n <- n_range[min_idx]
  cat("Candidate n per group (from coarse search):", candidate_n, "\n")
  
  # Refine search around the candidate
  n_fine <- seq(max(10, candidate_n - 10), candidate_n + 5)
  power_fine <- sapply(n_fine, function(n) compute_power(n, k, eta_sq, alpha)$power)
  
  fine_df <- data.frame(n_per_group = n_fine, power = power_fine)
  cat("\nFine search around candidate:\n")
  print(fine_df)
  
  # Find minimum n where power >= 0.80
  idx_min <- which(power_fine >= target_power)
  if (length(idx_min) > 0) {
    min_n_achieved <- n_fine[min(idx_min)]
    
    cat("\n=== RESULTS ===\n")
    cat("Minimum n per group achieving power >= 0.80:", min_n_achieved, "\n")
    
    # Compute detailed results for selected n
    selected <- compute_power(min_n_achieved, k, eta_sq, alpha)
    preceding <- compute_power(min_n_achieved - 1, k, eta_sq, alpha)
    
    cat("\nSelected design (n =", min_n_achieved, "):\n")
    cat("  Total sample size:", selected$N_total, "\n")
    cat("  Noncentrality parameter λ:", round(selected$lambda, 4), "\n")
    cat("  Critical F-value (df1=", selected$df1, ", df2=", selected$df2, "):", 
        round(selected$f_crit, 4), "\n")
    cat("  Achieved power:", round(selected$power, 4), "\n")
    
    cat("\nPreceding design (n =", min_n_achieved - 1, "):\n")
    cat("  Total sample size:", preceding$N_total, "\n")
    cat("  Noncentrality parameter λ:", round(preceding$lambda, 4), "\n")
    cat("  Critical F-value (df1=", preceding$df1, ", df2=", preceding$df2, "):", 
        round(preceding$f_crit, 4), "\n")
    cat("  Achieved power:", round(preceding$power, 4), "\n")
    
    cat("\n=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
    cat("Minimum integer participants per group:", min_n_achieved, "\n")
    cat("Achieved power:", round(selected$power, 4), "\n")
    cat("Power at preceding design (n =", min_n_achieved - 1, "):", round(preceding$power, 4), "\n")
  }
}

# Export result as JSON
result_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n_achieved, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(selected$power, 6), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(preceding$power, 6), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = selected$N_total, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "noncentrality_parameter", value = round(selected$lambda, 6), unit = "dimensionless")
  )
)
